title: fix(objectql): the create-side static-`readonly` strip judges the user-writable `managedBy` buckets (#15719)
body:
Fixes #15719

Clause-②: yes

Per the maintainer ruling's Execution paragraph (`5550128462`), verbatim:
「**Clause-② yes (create accept set moves on the affected objects); `@objectstack/objectql`
`minor` with the launch-window `**BREAKING**` banner and an adr-0087 disposition.**」
The ruling prescribes the declaration, the grade and the banner together, so the `minor`
here is the grade it named, not a bump taken to satisfy a gate. The create accept set
does move — for an app-authored object declaring a user-writable bucket on a name
outside `sys_` — even though, per the census below, no SHIPPED object changes behaviour.

The route adds no published key, no new error code and no new exported symbol: the
bucket list is a module-local `const` in `rule-validator.ts`, deliberately not exported
(which is also why `@objectstack/lint` narrows a mirror rather than importing one).

## What was asymmetric

`staticReadonlyInsertSubject` (`packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts`)
returned `null` for `managedBy` set to **anything**, so the CREATE path judged no
static `readonly` column on such an object, while the UPDATE path passed the raw
schema to `stripReadonlyFields` and stripped it. For a `managedBy` object a
non-system caller's create of a static `readonly` column was not stripped while the
same caller's update of the same column was.

The exclusion itself is sound — it was carried over from the deleted DataProtocol
ingress copy on ADR-0086 / #3004 grounds: those columns have their own 403 guards and
a silent strip must not swallow the payload the guard exists to reject. What was wrong
was the bucket list. `managedBy: 'system-data'` means "platform-defined schema,
**admin/user-writable data**" by its own definition, and `object.zod.ts` says in the
same breath that it "carries no such guard; its writes are adjudicated by the
delegated-admin gate / RLS / permission sets".

## The ruling this implements

Maintainer ruling on the card at `5550128462`, verbatim:

> **2, census first**: the create-side exclusion narrows to the buckets ADR-0086's
> 403-guard argument actually covers (platform internals and the `sys_` namespace);
> user-writable buckets such as `system-data` get the same static-`readonly` strip on
> create that they already [have on update]

## Census (a) — every `managedBy` bucket, classified

The classification axis is `object.zod.ts`'s own enum docblock, "Enforcement happens in
three places", item 3: which buckets have an engine write guard that fails closed on a
user-context generic write.

| bucket | its own refusal | create-side strip |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `engine-owned` | ADR-0103 engine-owned write guard | steps around it |
| `append-only` | ADR-0103, same guard (locked default) | steps around it |
| `better-auth` | ADR-0092 identity write guard | steps around it |
| `platform` | none — full user CRUD by default | **judges it** |
| `config` | none — admin-authored, writable by default | **judges it** |
| `system-data` | none — "admin/user-writable DATA" | **judges it** |

That table is the new exclusion list and it is in the docblock, as the ruling required.
It is pinned against `@objectstack/spec`'s enum by a test, so a seventh bucket fails
there instead of landing silently on the judging side.

## Census (b) — the shipped population, measured on this head

Every `.ts` object declaration in `packages/`, `apps/` and `examples/` carrying a
literal `managedBy`, parsed with the TypeScript AST (field definitions resolved through
the `Field.*(...)` builders, options object read from whichever argument carries it):

| reading | value |
|:--|--:|
| object declarations carrying `managedBy` | **81** |
| of those, named outside the `sys_` namespace | **0** |
| in the three now-judged buckets, carrying a static `readonly` column | **20** objects (`platform` 6, `config` 6, `system-data` 8) |
| static `readonly` columns on those (runtime-owned types excluded) | **64** |
| of those 64: ADR-0086 package-provenance family | **14** — `package_id`, `managed_by`, `customized`, `drift_status`, `drift_detail`, `is_system`, all on `config` objects |
| of those 64: `id` / `created_at` / `updated_at` stamps | **50** |
| in the three still-excluded buckets | **60** objects, **307** static `readonly` columns |

The ruling required the changeset to name the affected objects when (b) is greater than
zero. It is, and they are named there and here:

- `platform` (6 objects, 14 columns): `sys_attachment`, `sys_business_unit`,
  `sys_business_unit_member`, `sys_comment`, `sys_report_schedule`, `sys_saved_report`
- `config` (6 objects, 29 columns): `sys_capability`, `sys_email_template`,
  `sys_permission_set`, `sys_position`, `sys_sharing_rule`, `sys_webhook`
- `system-data` (8 objects, 21 columns): `sys_approval_delegation`,
  `sys_notification_preference`, `sys_notification_subscription`,
  `sys_notification_template`, `sys_position_permission_set`,
  `sys_user_permission_set`, `sys_user_position`, `sys_user_preference`

**Behaviour delta on the shipped population: zero.** Because no shipped `managedBy`
object is named outside `sys_` — every one of the 20 above included — the namespace
test, untouched here, keeps all of them exempt exactly as before. The narrowing reaches
app-authored objects only, which is the population the ruling is about.

⚠️ **Both halves or neither.** "Behaviour-free" alone overstates it: the population is
real and named above, and an app declaring one of those buckets on its own object gets
the strip. The population alone understates it: not one shipped object changes
behaviour on this release.

**The ruling's fallback does not apply.** It applies "only if the census shows the
user-writable buckets' readonly columns already carry their own 403 refusal". 14 of the
64 do; the other 50 are `id` / `created_at` / `updated_at` stamps that guard does not
reach. So the narrowing is the route, not option 1.

`sys_metadata_history.recorded_by` — seeded by a direct, non-system `engine.insert`
from `sys-metadata-repository.ts` — is doubly exempt (`engine-owned` bucket **and** the
`sys_` namespace) and is pinned as unaffected against the real exported object, not a
replica.

## What changed

- `packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts` — the predicate now tests the
  bucket against a module-local `PLATFORM_INTERNAL_MANAGED_BUCKETS` set instead of
  testing `managedBy` for truthiness. An **unrecognised** value is deliberately not
  read as platform-internal: the one legacy value that can still arrive is `'system'`,
  retired in protocol 17 (#3355) and converted to `'system-data'` — a judging bucket —
  so exempting unknowns would exempt precisely the rows that conversion targets.
- `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` — the create-path comment at the call site, which
  said "platform objects to their own 403 guards". Prose only; the strip's position
  after the `beforeInsert` hooks is untouched.
- `packages/objectql/src/readonly-strict-errors.ts` — the same sentence, which already
  cited this card.
- `packages/lint/src/validate-readonly-flow-writes.ts` — `buildInsertStripExemptObjects`
  is a deliberate mirror of the engine predicate (its own docblock: two readings that
  drift "produce two rules that disagree about the same field, and the disagreement is
  silent"). Narrowed in the same stroke and for the same reason; a lint that kept the
  wider exemption would go on suppressing create findings for a strip that now really
  happens. Shared by `validate-readonly-hook-writes.ts`, so both rules move together.
- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/authz-conformance.matrix.ts` — three sentences of the
  authz conformance record stated the strip steps around "a sys_-prefixed or managedBy
  object". Prose inside string literals; no assertion reads their content.

## ⛔ What was NOT changed

- **The UPDATE path.** The asymmetry is closed by moving CREATE toward UPDATE, never
  the other way. `stripReadonlyFields`'s two update call sites are untouched.
- **`beforeInsert`'s post-hook strip position** — settled by ruling C on #14147.
- **`managedBy`'s enum**, its `.describe()`, and every other authorable key.

## Evidence

**Red before / green after, in the real direction.** The unit file was written and
committed first, then run against the unmodified predicate:

- red, at `53dbf78738` (test only, fix not yet written):
  `Test Files 1 failed (1) · Tests 5 failed | 8 passed (13)`, each failure reading
  `AssertionError: platform holds the user's own data — the strip applies as it does on
  update: expected null not to be null`. The 8 that passed are the unchanged half —
  the three platform-internal buckets, the `sys_` cases, the `sys_metadata_history` pin
  and the enum partition.
- green, after the fix:
  `Test Files 3 passed (3) · Tests 219 passed (219)` over the new file plus
  `engine-insert-static-readonly-strip.test.ts` and `rule-validator.test.ts`.

**Package suites** (`pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter @objectstack/objectql --filter @objectstack/lint test`):

- `packages/objectql`: `Test Files 293 passed (293) · Tests 4909 passed (4909)`
- `packages/lint`: `Test Files 103 passed (103) · Tests 3717 passed (3717)`
- `@objectstack/dogfood` `test/authz-conformance.test.ts`: `Test Files 1 passed (1) · Tests 47 passed (47)`

**Typecheck** — both packages green, including their test layers
(`check:test-typecheck: OK` for each; objectql's ledger unchanged at 44 files / 242
errors / 69 pinned signatures, lint's at 2 / 6 / 2).

**Gate families** — derived with `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` from this
head's own change set and reconciled with `--ran`:
`70 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 68 run, 2 NOT-MEASURED`.
The two are `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `pnpm check:type-check-debt`, both
exit 3 = PREREQUISITE NOT MET: they read a fully built workspace, which is CI's run,
not a per-PR one. `pnpm check:lean-entry-closure` also refused at first for the same
class of reason and was re-run green after building `@objectstack/objectql`
(`2 published condition(s) measured from a real load`).

**Repo-wide `pnpm lint`** (`eslint . --no-inline-config`, the whole population, not a
narrowing): exit 0 at `c8092ff585`, the final commit.

**Control characters**: `pnpm check:nul-bytes` green, plus a direct
`grep -naP` sweep over all ten changed paths with a positive control that fired.

## The Clause-② declaration, and how it was settled

The dispatch claim declared `Clause-②: no`. The maintainer ruling comment
(`5550128462`) declared `yes` in its Execution paragraph, four lines below the headline
the claim quoted. This PR originally carried the claim's declaration and flagged the
disagreement rather than picking a side quietly; the dispatching seat then adjudicated
it and ruled **B — `Clause-②: yes` stands, with `minor` + the `**BREAKING**` banner +
an adr-0087 disposition, exactly as the ruling's Execution paragraph prescribed**
(https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/15719#issuecomment-5615057809).
The line at the top of this body carries that verdict. Nothing about the change itself
moved — this was a declaration-and-grade correction, applied as a new commit on top of
the reviewed head, with no rebase, amend or force-push.
